Lypovets Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Lypovets was a genuinely multi-faith town by the 1870s, its roughly 6,700 residents split among Catholic, Orthodox, and Jewish communities, each with its own house of worship. The Jewish community, first mentioned in the mid-18th century, grew to nearly half the town's population by 1897, owning much of its industry, including flour mills, tobacco factories, and a distillery. In the 1920s and 1930s, at least three separate Jewish agricultural collectives were established near the town, beginning with a 1924 commune that became a kolkhoz. About 200 Jewish men and boys were shot by September 1941, and most of the remaining community, numbering around 1,000, was murdered in the course of 1942. This cemetery, established in 1700 — a rare case of source agreement on an exact founding year — was fenced by the ESJF in 2019.
